name: China economy
summary: China's October CPI rose 0.7% and factory prices 5.7%; no deflation or contagion found, though demand is soft
state: China's consumer prices rose 0.7% in the year to October, flat on the month, while producer prices rose 5.7%, driven by energy and raw materials (National Bureau of Statistics via CGTN, 9 Nov). The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October, and Q3 growth of 4.5% is near the annual target. No new property-developer default wave or financial contagion was found as of 10 Nov, so Normal holds.
for_you: China's economy affects prices of goods the UK imports and the earnings of global companies. Rising factory-gate prices there can feed into import costs over time.
rubric_hit: Growth near target, no deflation (CPI +0.7%), no contagion found

sources.title: CGTN — China's October CPI up 0.7%, PPI rises 5.7%
People's Daily — China's CPI up 0.7 pct in October

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
